correctness.summary: The subgroup theorem checks independently. A_B is extension closed and weakly idempotent complete by additivity of Euler characteristic; shifts and contractible cones give a Frobenius exact category. The degreewise-split Ext^1 formula ⊕_n Hom(H^nX,H^{n+1}Y) is valid because every ambient extension of two A_B objects again has Euler characteristic in B. The stated stalk tests detect reverse ideal orthogonality. The object-ideal factorizations work for B=dZ by d-fold multiplicity and separately for B={0} by adjacent shifts. The explicit special ideal precover/preenvelope sequences have middle terms and kernels/cokernels in A_B with the claimed support. Finally, an object-special precover exists exactly when χ(H^{≤0}A)∈B, and dually for χ(H^{≥2}A); the two zero-Euler two-stalk witnesses show completeness fails on both sides for every proper subgroup. The Karoubi-envelope conclusion follows because every complex is a summand of a B-admissible one.

limitations: The parity specialization B=2Z is prior art.
The result is confined to bounded finite-dimensional complexes with degreewise split exact structure.
Older exact-category/K_0 literature may contain an equivalent abstract formulation under different terminology.
The global completeness-descent problem in arbitrary exact categories is not resolved.

originality.summary: Ren–Wang's September 2026 paper publicly treats only the even-total-cohomology/parity case, equivalently B=2Z, and Wang–Wang–Zhu give a different non-weakly-idempotent-complete counterexample. Targeted current searches did not locate an external theorem giving the full subgroup family, zero-Euler case, exact truncated-characteristic criteria, and object-completeness iff B=Z. Within SCOPE, this record precedes the duplicate `euler-characteristic-subgroup...` record by about 23 minutes and is the earlier repository provenance for the subgroup theorem. Originality remains qualified because an abstract K_0 formulation could exist in older exact-category literature.

scientific_value.summary: The result identifies the parity obstruction as one member of a complete Euler-subgroup family and gives an exact boundary for when ideal completeness descends to objects. The B={0} case and sharp object-specialness criteria show the mechanism is Euler/K_0 additivity rather than merely parity or fixed-multiplicity doubling.
